title: Stats App Common Envelope v1

uid.$comment: ADR-005 is ACCEPTED. Uniqueness is enforced in PostgreSQL by PRIMARY KEY (ts_device, uid), scoped PER PARTITION - a global unique index is not creatable on a table partitioned by ts_device (ADR-003, G2). No UUID format is enforced here: ZC guarantees uniqueness, not a format, and rejecting a non-UUID uid would reject valid data.

type.$comment: The five approved V1 stat types, as a closed enumeration. Without this, an unrecognised type validates cleanly against the envelope and is only caught later by routing - which means the 400 depends on where the record happens to fail rather than on the contract. STA-14A: adding a type adds a member here, and changes nothing about existing types.

processor.$comment: Unix epoch SECONDS. Bounded to 2000-01-01 .. 2100-01-01 so a millisecond timestamp fails validation with a 400 instead of silently landing ~53,000 years in the future where retention never reaches it. Answered 18 Aug 2026.

device.$comment: Unix epoch SECONDS. Bounded to 2000-01-01 .. 2100-01-01 so a millisecond timestamp fails validation with a 400 instead of silently landing ~53,000 years in the future where retention never reaches it. Answered 18 Aug 2026.

ts.$comment: ADR-004 is ACCEPTED: Stats App performs no timestamp normalisation and a record carrying ts.converter is INVALID. Other unknown ts members are still accepted under D14 (unknown-field policy).

$comment: additionalProperties stays true under the D14 unknown-field policy: unknown members are accepted and preserved rather than rejected. This is a deliberate decision (claude/CLAUDE.md §7), not a Jackson default - the alternative was considered and not chosen. Note the one asymmetry: ts.converter fails even though other unknown ts members pass, because its presence means the sender believes in a normalisation step this system does not perform (ADR-004).
